hook: Your anxiety response can activate faster than your conscious mind can register the trigger. Here's what that actually means.
topic: LeDoux's low road — fast threat processing explained
body:
**Your anxiety response can activate faster than your conscious mind can register the trigger.**

Your brain runs two processing pathways simultaneously. The slow one takes sensory information to the cortex — the reasoning part of your brain — where it's evaluated and contextualised before you respond.

The fast one bypasses the cortex entirely. It sends a rough, low-resolution version of the same signal directly to the amygdala — the part of the brain responsible for threat detection — before the cortex has finished its assessment.

The amygdala doesn't wait. Its job is not to be accurate. Its job is to be early.

So your heart rate, your chest tightness, your accelerated breathing — those can all be fully underway before your conscious mind has even completed the thought "wait, is this actually a problem?"

This is why telling yourself to calm down doesn't work. You're asking the cortex to override a system that already has a head start. The cortex is playing catch-up.

The correct entry point is the body — specifically, the breath — because that's the one input your nervous system accepts from you in real time.

The mechanism behind why — and the specific technique — is all in the free guide in my bio.
